scene.note: Your functions take what each call gives them, fill in the rest from their defaults, and give back a new value instead of changing the team's names.

steps.note: Rhona sends a message, and most of the time she does not say how urgent it is.
When the call gives no priority, the parameter takes its default; when it gives one, that one wins.
The pager shows the priority in capitals, then the message.
Sunday's exercise has a hill and a crew, and Ailsa's function takes two more values with defaults.
The meeting place keeps its default, and the one value after it is given by its parameter's name.
The exercise page goes out as routine, so nobody turns up at a run.
The rota calls leader_line with whoever leads tonight.
Inside, the function reads a name from the top of the file instead of what it was given.
Once it uses its own parameter, the rota names the right leader every night.
The rope count at the top cannot be changed from inside a function.
So take_ropes takes the count in as a value and works out what is left.
The new count comes back, and the line that called it stores it where the old one was.
